Z_N := (S_N − E S_N)/√Var(S_N) = (1/(σ√N)) Σ_{i=1}^N (X_i − μ) [cross-referenced Chapter 1 PDF page 5, printed page 9, Theorem 1.3.2].
ρ := E|X₁ − μ|³/σ³ [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14, sentence following the Berry–Esseen bound].
g ∼ N(0,1), meaning that g is standard normal [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14; cross-referenced Chapter 1 PDF page 5, printed page 9].
P{Y ≥ t} denotes an upper-tail probability, and the theorem takes the absolute value of the difference of two such probabilities [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14, displayed conclusion].

N is used as a positive sample size, although the phrase “for every N” does not explicitly spell out its domain [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14; cross-referenced Chapter 1 PDF page 5, printed page 9, S_N notation].

The displayed definitions of Z_N and ρ are meaningful as real-valued quotients only when σ is nonzero; the source does not separately state σ > 0 [cross-referenced Chapter 1 PDF page 5, printed page 9, normalization by σ√N; Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14, division by σ³].

Because the X_i are identically distributed, the moment computed using X₁ in the definition of ρ is representative of every summand [cross-referenced Chapter 1 PDF page 5, printed page 9, i.i.d. hypothesis; Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14, definition of ρ].

details: The estimate applies to every sample size N and every real threshold t [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14, explicit quantifiers].

The compared quantities are upper-tail probabilities at the same threshold t [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14, displayed formula].

The error is the absolute difference of those probabilities, not a one-sided difference and not a probability of a difference of random variables [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14, displayed formula].
The sum is centered by E S_N and divided by √Var(S_N), equivalently divided after termwise centering by σ√N [cross-referenced Chapter 1 PDF page 5, printed page 9, definition of Z_N].
The third absolute centered moment is normalized by σ³ [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14, definition of ρ].
The source gives the finite-N rate 1/√N with multiplicative factor exactly ρ in the displayed formulation [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14, displayed bound].

Only the standard normal marginal law of g is specified [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14, “g ∼ N(0,1)”].

No joint coupling or independence relation between g and the X_i is used by the conclusion, which compares separate marginal tail probabilities [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14, displayed formula].

The passage presents Theorem 2.1.3 as the Berry–Esseen central limit theorem and proceeds directly to discussion without supplying a proof in the cited passage [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14, structural transition from the theorem to “Thus the approximation error…”].

undebatable_constraints: The inherited i.i.d., common-mean, and common-variance setting of Theorem 1.3.2 must be retained; it cannot be discarded merely because Theorem 2.1.3 states it by citation [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14; cross-referenced Chapter 1 PDF page 5, printed page 9].
Z_N must be the normalized centered sum defined in Theorem 1.3.2, namely (S_N − E S_N)/√Var(S_N) = (1/(σ√N))Σ_{i=1}^N(X_i − μ) [cross-referenced Chapter 1 PDF page 5, printed page 9].
The conclusion must quantify over every N and every t ∈ R [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14].
The probability events must use the upper-tail relation ≥ at the same threshold t [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14, displayed formula].
The difference of the two tail probabilities must be enclosed in an absolute value [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14, displayed formula].
The right-hand side must be ρ/√N [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14, displayed formula].
ρ must be E|X₁ − μ|³/σ³; the absolute value, centering, exponent three, and normalization by σ³ are all essential [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14].
g must have the standard normal distribution N(0,1) [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14].

The source passage states this theorem without a local proof, so no proof content or stronger proved-in-chapter status may be attributed to the cited passage [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14, structural presentation].

contract_plain_english: For an i.i.d. sequence with common mean μ and variance σ², let S_N be its first-N sum and let Z_N be the centered sum divided by σ√N. For every positive sample size N and every real threshold t, the upper-tail probability of Z_N differs in absolute value from the upper-tail probability of a standard normal g by at most ρ/√N, where ρ = E|X₁ − μ|³/σ³ [Chapter 2 PDF page 3, printed page 14, Theorem 2.1.3; inherited definitions and hypotheses from cross-referenced Chapter 1 PDF page 5, printed page 9, Theorem 1.3.2].
